Subject: Post-call: Performance tradeoffs & serving playbook (Rivermark)

Hi Samira — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our 45m discovery and a proposed plan so we keep momentum. Pulling a few highlights below and suggested next steps.

Key goals you mentioned
- Latency: p95 generation <= 150ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens), 250ms for medium (512–2k) — streaming acceptable for long responses
- Throughput: sustained 180–250 req/s across peak windows; occasional spikes to 500 req/s for short bursts
- Concurrency: expected concurrency ~80 active users (ends up ~300 concurrent sessions with multiplexing)
- Streaming: need partial tokens delivered within 120ms of generation start; SSE acceptable, some clients prefer chunked JSON frames
- Cost sensitivity: procurement budget targets ~ $0.40 per 1k inference tokens (high-level)

Primary risk areas we flagged
- Tight p95 targets vs cost constraints on 70B models
- Streaming requirements reduce some batching efficiency
- Multi-tenant cache TTL and cold-starts for rare prompts

Suggested playbook (what we can try in PoC)
1) Qualification matrix: run 3 scenarios (short/text-complete, long/streamed narrative, reranking microbatch). See attached rivermark_slo_matrix.xlsx
2) Baseline profile on your sample prompts (we'll run hosted endpoints with matching seq lengths)
3) Levers to test: continuous batching (small max latency budget), prefix KV caching for top-10k prompts, int8 quantized variants for cost tradeoffs, and a model variant fallback policy
4) Streaming config: SSE with 120ms chunk target, backpressure at 20 tokens per frame
5) Acceptance criteria: p95 latency within target on 90% of scenarios, cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your budget

Next steps I propose
- We run a 2-week perf qualification PoC (we provide test harness + 100k free tokens) — timeline: start Mon Apr 26, results week-of May 10
- Karthik to provide initial perf/cost estimates and a runbook for the PoC
- Book a 30m follow-up to review matrix and baseline results (suggest May 12)

Attachments: rivermark_slo_matrix.xlsx, call-recording-0418.mp3

Thanks — I cc'ed Monica for procurement/contract sync. If that timeline works, I'll send a short SOW and test-access next week.

Lauren / team / Samira — attached is a short technical brief (k-iyer-perf-estimates.pdf). Highlights / quick answers below.

Summary of levers (glossary)
- Continuous batching: keep per-GPU batching active with a max latency budget (e.g., 40ms for short prompts). Improves throughput ~2–3x for small requests; adds headroom to hit throughput targets while preserving p95 if budget tuned.
- Prefix KV caching: cache KV states for commonly seen prompts/top-10k queries. Reduces repeated attention compute for cached prefixes, cutting cost ~20–45% for high cache-hit workloads. TTL and invalidation policy matter.
- Quantization profiles: int8/4-bit quantization reduces memory and inference FLOPs. Expect 30–60% cost reduction vs fp16 at some accuracy tradeoff; int8 usually safe for generation, 4-bit requires evals.
- Model variants / fallback policy: run highest-quality (70B fp16) as primary for critical flows, but route 60–80% of calls to 13B-quant for non-critical prompts to meet unit cost targets. Can implement deterministic routing by prompt class.

Estimated P95 latency (approx, hosted Redwood config)
- Short (<=512 tokens): 70B fp16 ~140ms p95 (no streaming), 13B-quant ~85ms p95. With continuous batching budget=40ms, delta ~ +10–25ms depending on load.
- Long/streamed (2k tokens): streamed first-byte p95 ~110–150ms for both variants; end-to-end completion longer but streaming satisfies UX SLOs.
- Reranking microbatch (batch size 8–16): batching provides 3–6x throughput improvements; latency per item ~40–90ms depending on CPU vs GPU overheads.

Cost impact (very rough)
- Baseline (70B fp16) cost per 1k tokens: ~$1.20.
- 13B quant baseline: ~$0.32 per 1k tokens.
- With caching + continuous batching mix (50% cache-hit, 60% routed to 13B-quant): effective cost ~ $0.28–0.45 per 1k tokens depending on hit rates.

Streaming recommendations
- Use SSE with chunked JSON frames; aim for ~120ms first-frame target, subsequent frames every 70–120ms. Keep payloads ~200–400 bytes to avoid browser backpressure.

PoC runbook (short)
- Week 1: baseline profiling on sample prompts (short/long/rerank) — measure cold start and steady state
- Week 2: enable KV caching + continuous batching + quantized model variant routing, measure cost/latency effects
- Deliverable: perf matrix + recommendations and config snippets for Redwood Dedicated or Hosted routes

I'll join the May 12 review. If procurement needs a hard cap for PoC, Redwood can set a spend limit and we can apply trial credit to overages.

— Karthik Iyer
